understanding: The selected implementation is the repository's Paxos variant, instantiated by runReplica after master registration. Source shows per-instance ballots, command batches, prepare and accept reply counters, full and short commit handlers, a separate command-execution loop, and recovery requests for blocked instances. The constructor enables execution and initializes Durability to false and direct replies to true through the embedded replica. Decision handlers and execution have been read, but their dispatch, proposal admission, ballot generation, broadcast selection, and transport ownership remain unread. This inventory describes local state transitions and observations, not established consensus guarantees. In particular, reply counting, command selection after prepare replies, and interpretation of short commits require their actual producer and dispatch context before stronger semantic conclusions.

target_profile.system_boundary: Paxos replica implementation with built-in replica transport, quorum helpers, application state, client interfaces, and master-based startup and authority interfaces. Other protocol implementations are deployment alternatives outside this initial Paxos workset.
protocol_contexts: Instances are indexed by int32 and contain cmds, bal, vbal, status, and optional leader bookkeeping.
Replica-wide context includes IsLeader, maxRecvBallot, per-participant defaultBallot, smallestDefaultBallot, crtInstance, and executedUpTo.
ReadQuorumSize returns N-F; WriteQuorumSize returns F+1. runReplica derives F from configured replica addresses, while the embedded replica derives N from the master's returned address list.
external_interfaces: Master.Register supplies replica identity, node list, readiness, and initial leader indication.
HTTP RPC exposes the constructed replica, including BeTheLeader.
Registered serializable messages include Prepare, Accept, Commit, CommitShort, PrepareReply, and AcceptReply.
Client proposals carry ClientId, CommandId, command, and timestamp.
Application state supports PUT, GET, and SCAN command representations.
Conditional persistence calls use the built-in *os.File StableStore.
ownership: runReplica selects and constructs the protocol implementation.
The embedded replica owns peer connections, RPC table, proposal channel, state, and StableStore.
Paxos New launches r.run; dispatch and additional goroutine startup remain unread.
executeCommands accesses instance state and publishes recovery requests independently of the handler code; its actual launch and synchronization need inspection.
The master owns registration and reported leader information.
selection_injection: The case-insensitive Protocol value selects paxos.New in runReplica.
paxos.New receives identity, participant addresses, initial leadership, F, configuration, and logger.
paxos.New invokes replica.New with thrifty=false, exec=true, and lread=false.
Built-in transport, storage, quorum, and state implementations remain within the analysis boundary; constructor parameters do not externalize these responsibilities.
variants: The repository advertises SwiftPaxos, Paxos, N²Paxos, CURP, Fast Paxos, and EPaxos; only the Paxos branch is selected here.
The embedded constructor initializes Dreply=true and Durable=false; later changes to these fields are unknown.
Full and short commit messages follow distinct handlers.
With Dreply enabled, eligible client replies are sent after Execute; with Dreply disabled, handleAcceptReply can reply with an empty value after marking COMMITTED.
Master registration can use an explicitly configured leader or latency-based selection.
Client SendProposal supports single-destination and broadcast modes; activation for this deployment is unknown.
unknowns: Actual proposal admission, dispatch serialization, startup behavior, ballot construction, and broadcast recipient selection.
Whether later code enables durability or changes direct-reply behavior.
Transport delivery, duplicate handling, reconnect behavior, and message sender attribution.
Supported crash/restart contract and any durable restore path.
Whether runtime participant changes exist beyond startup registration.
No correctness, replay, or calibration evidence is supplied; offline compilation capability establishes none of these.

activities.purpose: Process committed instance commands into application effects.
activities.realization_summary: executeCommands advances from executedUpTo+1 only through instances with non-nil commands and COMMITTED status. It executes every command when direct replies and local client bookkeeping are available; otherwise it executes only PUT commands.

activities.purpose: Retain instance state and conditionally write recovery-related representations.
activities.realization_summary: Instances are retained in memory. Conditional helpers write ballot/status bytes, marshal commands, and call Sync. Durable defaults to false. The helpers do not inspect storage return values, so calls do not establish successful durable completion.
unknowns: Restore format and instance identity reconstruction

activities.purpose: Associate client operations with proposals and completion replies.
activities.realization_summary: Clients attach a generated ClientId and incrementing CommandId. Paxos replies either during execution or after local commit depending on Dreply. Full commit reception can requeue local proposals. End-to-end retry and completion interpretation remain partial.
